## Core Terms and Variables

This section declares the notation used by the expansion chapter. The physical work performed by these quantities is developed in the sections that follow.

### Inherited momentum quantities

The fermic momentum scale is $p_f$. The bosic momentum has vector form $\vec p$ and nonnegative magnitude

$$
p=|\vec p|.
$$

For an oriented unit direction $\hat{k}$, its signed projection is

$$
p_k=\vec p\mathbin{\cdot}\hat{k}.
$$

The inertial core-momentum magnitude may be written as a function of $p$,

$$
M(p)=\sqrt{p_f^2+p^2}.
$$

The corresponding positive shell readings along the chosen orientation are

$$
p_k^\pm=M(p)\pm\frac12p_k.
$$

The superscripts $+$ and $-$ label opposed positive readings. For a selected orientation, ADMC conserves one shell reading per particle. Reversing the orientation exchanges $p_k^+$ and $p_k^-$. The two readings may be displayed together for comparison or inversion; they are not two simultaneous terms in one particle's ADMC contribution.

### Translation yield

The chapter's expansion quantity is

$$
\chi(t),
$$

called **translation yield**. It is a dimensionless factor associated with the displacement produced by directed momentum at epoch $t$.

Emission and observation values are written

$$
\chi_e=\chi(t_e),
\qquad
\chi_o=\chi(t_o).
$$

The observation epoch may be used as the normalization point,

$$
\chi_o=1,
$$

unless another normalization is stated.

The defining translation map is

$$
\dot x_k(t)=\chi(t)c\frac{p_k}{M(p)}.
$$

Here $t$ is the common background-history parameter used to label the homogeneous yield state, and $x_k$ is the corresponding translation coordinate along $\hat{k}$. The dot denotes differentiation with respect to that parameter. These variables provide the propagation bookkeeping; an operational measurement additionally involves the local rods and clocks used at the endpoints. Here $c$ retains its inherited role as the intrinsic local propagation scale. The epoch-dependent factor is $\chi(t)$.

The fractional yield-change rate is

$$
H_\chi(t)=-\frac{\dot\chi(t)}{\chi(t)}.
$$

### Signal labels

Observed wavelength redshift is denoted by

$$
1+z=\frac{\lambda_o}{\lambda_e}.
$$

For two neighboring signal features, $\delta t_e$ and $\delta t_o$ denote their emission and reception separations in the background parameter $t$. The durations reported against the emitter's and observer's local clock standards are written $\Delta t_e$ and $\Delta t_o$. The propagation argument first relates the background endpoint separations; the signal comparison then states when they may be read as the corresponding local durations.
